data.narrative:
Wiliot is a Series C-stage semiconductor company that has raised $364M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across Chips & Semiconductors—3 public names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private entities. Same-stage, same-sector private comparables include Etched ($5.0B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and DEEPX ($529M).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.7x multiplier to the $364M raised proxy, yielding $619M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-sector Series C private comparables produces a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $529M to $5.0B. The dispersion reflects meaningful differences in traction, market positioning, and investor thesis across the cohort.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $526M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The wide range reflects structural uncertainty: stage-progression implies a more conservative floor anchored to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects substantial variance in how the market prices competing architectures and go-to-market strategies within the sector. Key uncertainties include Wiliot's capital efficiency relative to peers, product-market fit trajectory, and customer concentration.
